title: Extract payment policy behind a module boundary
requirement: Move payment recognition, fee, reference and authorization policy from internal/checkout to a new internal/payments package. Payments owns PaymentKnown, PaymentFee, PaymentReference (unexported camelCase equivalents are permitted), Authorize and its own Authorization/error contract. It must not depend directly or transitively on checkout, inventory, pricing, shipping, catalog, app, reservations or refunds. Keep checkout.Authorize and checkout.Authorization/checkout.Error working for existing callers. checkout.Authorize must delegate to payments.Authorize; checkout must no longer define the three payment helpers. Preserve all HTTP responses, fee/reference behavior, public APIs and tests. Ordinary Go errors and aliases or wrappers are permitted when they preserve the contract; no nominal error/record conversion is required. Do not add an unused package or re-export policy that still lives in checkout. Behavioral, public API and structural outcomes are scored separately.
scope: One independent change to the supplied baseline; implement and verify without a human review gate.
acceptance: Behavior is checked through HTTP against the task and unchanged baseline contracts. Payment-boundary additionally has an explicit structural check. Add or update meaningful public tests.
limits: Do not change AGENTS.md, task.json or the Go module identity. Use the declared isolated tool environment. Add meaningful tests; implement, audit and verify without waiting for human source review.
